subject: Recap + Exception Ask: HearthHealth pilot governance, stakeholders & SLA/discount
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Recap + Exception Ask: HearthHealth pilot governance, stakeholders & SLA/discount

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery call with HearthHealth (Samantha/Security/Procurement). They liked the demo but have a nonstandard buying path and a couple of asks that will need internal clearance. Notes and a proposed mutual action plan attached. TL;DR asks: 1) 8-week pilot with 20% pilot discount; 2) temporary SLA variance (pilot SLA 99.9% vs our standard 99.95); 3) allow customer-managed KMS for key isolation (BYOK) for pilot; 4) procurement wants 30-day data retention by default and audit logging proof.

Stakeholder map (from call):
- Economic / exec sponsor: Samantha Cole (VP Product, HearthHealth) — controls budget and pilot signoff.
- Security / technical buyer: Alex Rivera (InfoSec lead) — will own BYOK and audit evidence.
- Procurement: procurement@hearthhealth.com (Tom Briggs) — will run PO/contract stages, standard 30-day net terms for pilot.
- Solutions / PM: internal champion is Tom (Product), but Samantha is the final decision maker.

Current asks for internal approval:
- Pilot discount: request 20% off list for an 8-week pilot (recommended: approve up to 15% without exec).
- SLA variance: accept 99.9% for pilot period with a rollback to standard SLA at GA.
- Security exception: allow BYOK (customer-managed KMS) limited to pilot environment and audited via our audit logs export.

Why this matters: HearthHealth is a strategic health-tech prospect with potential for dedicated capacity next year; the pilot is fairly large (approx 3M tokens/month expected during pilot peak). We should balance commercial flexibility vs precedent.

Next steps I propose: 1) Internal approval thread for commercial/SLA/security exceptions (this email). 2) Draft an addendum with limited pilot terms to send to procurement (Laura, can you draft?). 3) SE/Eng (Dev) to confirm feasibility and list what telemetry/log artifacts we can ship for audit (Dev — can you confirm today?). 4) If approved, I'll send a one-page exceptions package to Neha for sign-off before we reply to Samantha.

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), HH-proposed-MAP.xlsx (timeline + deliverables).

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap + Exception Ask: HearthHealth pilot governance, stakeholders & SLA/discount

Hannah — good write-up. +1 on moving quickly. A couple of thoughts:
- Discount: I'm okay to approve up to 15% for a time-bound pilot. 20% is a bit deep; would rather protect margin. We can tie the additional 5% to an outcome (e.g., commit to a Dedicated proof-of-concept within 90 days if metrics hit).
- SLA: 99.9% for an 8-week pilot seems reasonable if it's time-limited and we don't expose it as a new standard. Need legal to approve liability language.
- BYOK: This is doable for a pilot but we need to validate whether our hosted instance can support a customer KMS connection without adding significant ops work. Dev — is that a quick enable?

If legal/ops OK, I recommend we offer a 15% baseline and a performance milestone to get to 20%. I can take point on commercial messaging to the customer.

Ben
Account Director | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 10:05 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> If legal/ops OK, I recommend we offer a 15% baseline and a performance milestone to get to 20%. I can take point on commercial messaging to the customer.

Hannah / Ben — technical quick-check: BYOK for a hosted pilot is feasible but with caveats. We can support a customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest, but:
- It requires a short integration window (approx 3 business days) and coordination with customer security to exchange public keys and rotate certs.
- Audit logs: we can provide request-level logs and token usage summaries via a secure S3 export and a signed checksum; full raw telemetry will need opt-in.
- SLA: achieving 99.9% vs 99.95% is not a technical issue; it's primarily a contract/ops exposure. For pilot traffic patterns, we can guarantee throughput.

I can put together a short tech note for Laura to include in the addendum describing BYOK scope and what auditing artifacts we can deliver. I can do this by EOD.

Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap + Exception Ask: HearthHealth pilot governance, stakeholders & SLA/discount

Thanks — I'll draft a one-page pilot addendum that: 1) limits the 99.9% SLA to the 8-week pilot term only; 2) specifies BYOK is limited to pilot environment and that key custody never leaves the customer's KMS; 3) enumerates the audit artifacts we can provide and the delivery method (S3 export + signed hash). I'll loop Legal for the liability language.

For the discount, let's propose: 15% off list plus a 5% performance bonus contingent on conversion to Dedicated within 90 days and meeting a token-usage threshold. That makes it easier to get commercial approval.

Laura
Sr. Manager, Contracts & Pricing | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + Exception Ask: HearthHealth pilot governance, stakeholders & SLA/discount

Hannah — looks good. I approve the following internal recommendation to present to HearthHealth (please confirm you want me to sign off formally after you send):
- Offer: 8-week pilot, 15% baseline discount with a conditional 5% performance rebate if they commit to Dedicated within 90 days and meet the agreed usage metric.
- SLA: allow 99.9% for the pilot only; include explicit rollback to standard SLA at GA.
- BYOK: approve as pilot-limited feature; include a short tech appendix (Dev) describing integration steps and evidence we'll provide.
- Data retention: comply with 30-day retention during pilot; provide audit logs as specified.

Hannah — once Laura has the addendum draft and Dev has the tech note, send me the one-page exceptions package and I'll sign for Sales approval. If Procurement pushes net terms beyond our standard, don't accept changes without pre-cleared legal review.

Neha Kapoor
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
